answer: Trust propagates through bounded random walks on the attestation graph, so voting weight reflects reachable, repeatedly supported nodes rather than raw identity count. A sybil cluster joined to honest nodes by a sparse cut has low conductance; when weight is normalized to walk flow from trusted seeds, its aggregate share is limited by that boundary, with min-cut transitivity bounds preventing internal attestations from amplifying it. A vine of fake identities cannot turn a haven into a tundra of unchecked influence.
